land.text: Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a, occupied in 989 and shared with the Buyid governor of Mosul

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by the Hamdanid, Mirdasid and Numayrid dynasties.

land.text: half of the dependencies of Mosul, granted by the Buyid governor in 989/990; the whole city from 996
Mosul, taken by the Seljuk Kerbogha in October 1096

successors.note: Infobox: succeeded by the Seljuk Empire, the Mujallid Emirate, the Emirate of Ja'bar and the Emirate of Hit (Uqaylid branches; Qal'at Ja'bar and Raqqa until 1169).

capitals.name: Mosul
capitals.note: Infobox capital; the main line was centred on Mosul "for more than a century". Branches at Nusaybin and Jazirat ibn Umar, Qal'at Ja'bar, Raqqa and Hit.

rulers.note: the Qirwash page says he died on 27 October 1052; the Uqaylid page gives him to 1050 and Baraka 1050-1052

rulers.note: killed June 1085 fighting Suleiman ibn Qutalmish

rulers.name: Ibrahim ibn Quraysh

correction.text: Diyar Rabi'a (Nusaybin) and the Uqaylid half of Mosul's dependencies

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Uqaylid row): "occupied Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a in 989" (infobox: founded 990) and "forced the Buwayhid governor of Mosul to grant him half of his dependencies". The page gives no area; Nusaybin as the seat of Diyar Rabi'a is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Mosul province, Diyar Rabi'a and Kufa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Al-Muqallad forced its Buwayhid governor out in 996"; Kufa and Hilla (Jami'yan) came with Mosul under a treaty with Baha' al-Dawla.
New keyframe: Kufa "reassigned to him in 1005/6", but "a campaign against it in 1006/7 failed"; the pages do not say when it was finally lost, 1007 is bridging.

correction.text: Mosul province, Diyar Rabi'a and al-Rahba on the Euphrates

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: al-Rahba seized from its pro-Fatimid governor in 1008/9 (the Mirdasid page says Salih ibn Mirdas captured it in 1008 and made it his capital 1014-1024).

New keyframe, the long middle of the emirate (Qirwash's Anbar and al-Mada'in, held in 1010 when he read the Fatimid sermon there, and Tikrit before about 1020 are not drawn: no page dates them as gains).
New keyframe: "Muslim ibn Quraysh took it [Aleppo] from the Mirdasids in June 1080"; Harran taken from the Numayrids in 1081.

correction.text: Mosul, Diyar Rabi'a, Aleppo and Harran
Mosul province and Diyar Rabi'a under Seljuk supremacy

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Malik Shah took it [Aleppo] in 1086"; the Malik-Shah page adds Harran and Qal'at Ja'bar. Mosul stayed Uqaylid under Seljuk supremacy until October 1096.

region.text: Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a, with half of the dependencies of Mosul

ledger.note: 990: the Banu Uqayl take Mosul's countryside. The Uqaylids 'occupied Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a in 989', then Muhammad ibn al-Musayyab 'forced the Buwayhid governor of Mosul to grant him half of his dependencies' (infobox: 'Founded: 990'); the Buyids had first granted them Diyar Bakr land as a buffer against the Kurdish rebel Badh ibn Dustak.
996: al-Muqallad takes Mosul and Kufa. 'Al-Muqallad forced its Buwayhid governor out in 996'; 'Kufa and Hilla (Jami'yan)' came with Mosul under a treaty with Baha' al-Dawla.
1007: Kufa lost. The Qirwash page: the Buyids took Kufa away after 1002 and reassigned it to him in 1005/6, but 'a campaign against it in 1006/7 failed'; the year of the final loss is bridging.

region.text: al-Rahba, the town on the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1008: Qirwash seizes al-Rahba. 'Seized from its pro-Fatimid governor in 1008/9.' The Mirdasid page has Salih ibn Mirdas capturing al-Rahba in 1008.

region.text: al-Rahba, the capital of Salih ibn Mirdas 1014-1024

ledger.note: 1014: al-Rahba passes to the Mirdasids. Salih ibn Mirdas escaped imprisonment in 1014, rallied the Kilab and made al-Rahba his capital (1014-1024); the page does not say it took the town from the Uqaylids.

region.text: Aleppo, whose inhabitants offered to hand it over

ledger.note: 1080: Muslim ibn Quraysh takes Aleppo. 'Muslim ibn Quraysh took it from the Mirdasids in June 1080, after its inhabitants offered to hand it over.' The Mirdasid page: 'in 1080, prompted by Sabiq ... Sharaf al-Dawla Muslim took over Aleppo'.
1081: Muslim takes Harran from the Numayrids. 'Harran: Taken from the Numayrids in 1081' (Muslim ibn Quraysh page: 'in the following year').

1086: Malik-Shah takes Aleppo. 'Aleppo: ... Malik Shah took it in 1086.' The Malik-Shah page lists Aleppo, Antioch, Edessa, Harran and Qal'at Ja'bar among the places taken in his 1086 Syrian campaign (no months).

1096: Kerbogha takes Mosul and the Uqaylid emirate ends. Infobox: 'Fall of Mosul, October 1096'; 'Kerbogha took the city in late 1096, ending Uqaylid rule'. Branches survived at Hit, Qal'at Ja'bar and Raqqa (to 1169).

wars.name: Uqaylid takeover of Mosul from the Buyids
wars.outcome: The Uqaylids occupied Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a in 989, defeated Badh ibn Dustak, turned on the Hamdanids and forced the Buyid governor to grant them half of his dependencies; al-Muqallad drove the governor out in 996.

wars.name: Oghuz attack on Mosul (1044)
wars.outcome: The Oghuz occupied and sacked Mosul but Qirwash expelled them with Mazyadid support (the Qirwash page: he and Dubays defeated the Oghuz at Ra's al-Ayil on 21 April 1044).

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Aleppo (1080)
wars.outcome: Muslim ibn Quraysh took Aleppo from the Mirdasids in June 1080 and Harran from the Numayrids in 1081.

wars.name: Muslim ibn Quraysh against Suleiman ibn Qutalmish
wars.outcome: Suleiman took Antioch in December 1084 and refused the tribute Muslim claimed; Muslim was killed fighting him in June 1085 after his Turkoman troops switched sides. No Uqaylid border moved.

wars.name: Seljuk campaign in Syria and the Jazira (1086)
wars.outcome: Malik-Shah took Aleppo, Antioch, Edessa and Harran; the Uqaylids kept Mosul under Seljuk supremacy.
wars.note: The Malik-Shah page also has the Seljuks attacking Muslim's headquarters and taking Marwanid Diyar Bakr, undated and in an order that contradicts Muslim's death in 1085; not used for a border move.

wars.name: Battle of al-Muday' (1093)
wars.outcome: Ibrahim ibn Quraysh and his uncle were killed on 2 April 1093 outside Mosul; Ali ibn Muslim held the emirate to 1096.

certainty.note: No treaty lines survive on the pages: the emirate is a set of cities (Mosul, Nusaybin, al-Rahba, Aleppo, Harran) with desert and steppe between them. The Mosul core is firmer than the Euphrates and Syrian outliers.

notes: Cliopatria has no Uqaylid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. The page gives no area. Disagreements: founding 989 (occupation of Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a) vs 990 (infobox) vs 'Unification: 1000'; Qirwash's death 1050 (Uqaylid page, Baraka 1050-1052) vs 27 October 1052 (Qirwash page); al-Rahba taken by Qirwash 1008/9 (Qirwash page) vs by Salih ibn Mirdas 1008 (Mirdasid page). The Malik-Shah page's Syria/Jazira paragraph is undated and out of order (it has Muslim fleeing to Diyarbakir and later pardoned, then killed), so no Mosul loss is written for 1086. Not written as events: Kufa shuffles 1002-1007 (only the bridging loss in 1007), Anbar and al-Mada'in (held 1010), Tikrit (lost to Rafi' ibn al-Husayn c. 1020 with Buyid help, never dated as a gain), Baghdad control after 1012, nominal subservience to the Buyids (treaty, undated) and acknowledgement of Seljuk supremacy under Quraysh (1052-1061, undated), the Byzantine tribute in the lead, the Jazirat ibn Umar and Nusaybin lines (Badran's holding is the only mention of Nisibis), the branches at Qal'at Ja'bar/Raqqa (to 1169 by Zengids), Hit and the Mujallid emirate. Counterparts needing dossiers: mirdasid-dynasty (written here), numayrid-dynasty (Harran, Raqqa; about 990-1081), marwanids-of-diyar-bakr (written here), banu-mazyad (written here if budget allowed), oghuz-turks (ia-01). 'Nusaybin' and 'Kufa' resolve; al-Rahba is a coordinate radius because the gazetteer lacks it (gazetteer_names_needed: Rahba, Mayyafariqin, Akhlat, Cizre, Hasankeyf, Jazirat ibn Umar).
